title: Fast matrix permanents over F_3 / F_5 / F_7 via packed bipedal arithmetic
description:
## Context Reproduce and beat the results of Scheinerman, *Fast computation of permanents over F₃ via F₂ arithmetic* (arxiv 2407.20205v2, Aug 2024). The paper uses a "bipedal" map encoding F₃ⁿ as a pair of F₂ⁿ vectors, implements add/sub/mul/div in 1–6 bitwise ops, and combines this with Ryser's permanent formula in Gray-code order to achieve a reported 86.9× speedup over a naive Ryser implementation in Julia, single-thread, on a 4.20 GHz desktop. The paper does not exploit SIMD, multicore, or GPU. This epic introduces a new top-level workspace crate `gf2-algebra` that: 1. Reproduces the paper's `permanent_mod3` algorithm in Rust as an in-tree baseline. 2. Beats it by ≥ 50× single-thread via AVX2 (and AVX-512 where available) bipedal SIMD kernels in `gf2-kernels-simd`. 3. Adds rayon parallel scaling and HIP/ROCm GPU kernels in `gf2-kernels-hip`. 4. Generalises to F₅ and F₇ via best-effort encoding research (`type:simulation` children R1, R2). 5. Mechanically verifies (Lean4 via Charon/Aeneas) the bipedal F₃ arithmetic and Ryser's formula on the project's `FiniteField` trait, scoped to the bounded n ≤ 63 single-`u64` regime. 6. Produces a publication-grade benchmark artefact (criterion + plots + reproducible scripts). The full design is in the linked design doc, including the wave plan (W0..W7, ~48 children), the `PackedField` trait surface, the F₃/F₅/F₇ encoding plans, the hardware envelope (dev host: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, AVX2 only — AVX-512 paths are `[aspirational]`), and the risk register. ## Non-goals - General-purpose char-3 linear algebra (det, rank, char-poly, Smith normal form) — natural follow-up, out of scope here. - Permanents over F₂ (= determinant; already trivial via existing rank/RREF code). - Primes p ≥ 11. - Proof of unbounded-n Ryser (requires formalising arbitrary-arity sums; would explode V2 scope). - Reproducing the paper's n=50 / 832-CPU-hour 128-core run literally — we'll do a smaller analogous run that demonstrates the speedup factor. ## Success Criteria 1. [hard] A new workspace crate `gf2-algebra` exists, builds clean under `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --release --profile ci`, and is registered in the workspace `Cargo.toml`. 2. [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3` produces values bit-identical to the generic `permanent_ryser` over `Fp<3>` on 1000 random matrices for every n ∈ {1..16} and on 100 random matrices for n=20, 24, 28, 32. 3. [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3` (single-thread, AVX2 path) runs n=36 random {-1,0,1} matrices ≥ 50× faster than the in-tree `permanent_mod3_reference` (faithful Rust port of paper Julia) on the same machine. 4. [aspirational] Same comparison vs the paper's published Julia number on a documented Zen 4/5 reference host: ≥ 50× speedup at n=36. 5. [hard for n ≥ 28] `permanent_bipedal3` parallel scaling factor is ≥ 0.85× per physical core up to the host's physical core count, measured by simulation child S2. 6. [hard] F₅ and F₇ packed permanents return values matching `permanent_ryser` over the corresponding `Fp

` on 1000 random matrices for n ∈ {1..14}. 7. [hard] Lean4 proof V1 (bipedal F₃ correctness vs `Fp<3>`) builds with `lake build` and contains no `sorry`. 8. [hard] Lean4 proof V2 (Ryser's formula on `FiniteField`, bounded n ≤ 63) builds with `lake build` and contains no `sorry`. 9. [hard] A reproducible benchmark artefact (S6) lives in `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/`, with criterion JSONs, hardware fingerprint, seed pins, and `scripts/permanent-repro.sh` runs end-to-end. 10. [aspirational] GPU permanent crossover at n ≥ 40 for F₃ on gfx1030 (S5). 11. [hard] Root `CLAUDE.md` and `ROADMAP.md` are updated to reference `gf2-algebra`. 12. [hard] `cargo run -p gf2-algebra --example permanent_demo --release` produces the headline numbers from S6 within ±5%.
